deviations.rule: R1 adds each entry below. Verdict rule (COUNTS): COUNTS: a completed read of real market data (bars, quotes, trades, snapshots, auctions, screeners, corporate actions or news served by a market-data API; OPRA; FINRA short volume), or a real paper or broker session that consumed it, whose data dates fall inside the window and which no known_reads item covers. Window membership is judged by the dates of the data read, not the run date. OUT (a market-data classification only; it never removes a required inspection binding, which D6.3 makes for every recorded in-window read): synthetic content (made-up data; a real record kept as a test fixture is not synthetic), not run, data dated outside the window, no market data (filings, documents, account state), covered by a known_reads item, a local re-read inside a bound item's scope, or a wrapper of another record. Access kind: data_read: the record shows only data, counts or coverage. result_inspected: the record shows per-case results (fills, realized P&L, flags, ranks). outcome_selected: names were chosen by a realized outcome (a gain or move threshold, a ranking by realized return, a known mover). Where one scope mixes kinds and the record cannot split it, the stronger kind is proposed and flagged. Where a record cannot split a scope, the stronger access kind is bound. Step 3's conservative rule (PREREGISTRATION.md:51-52) applies to every universe-wide entry, whatever its access kind.

(4) outcome_selected is applied across a whole universe where its selected subset is private or partly named. (5) Code-derived request windows are bound as derived; an endpoint the record does not determine is recorded as unknown (frozen D1, deviations.json rule.unknown), never replaced by the window endpoint. (6) The market-data OUT classification (synthetic content, runs that observed nothing, data outside the window, wrapper records) is separate from the required inspection bindings: a real record kept as a test fixture is not synthetic, and every recorded in-window read is bound (D6.3) whatever its market-data verdict.
